why:
Most commands work as written. `npm test` maps to `node --test` in package.json. bin/greet.js exists, so `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada`, `node bin/greet.js Ada` and `node bin/greet.js` with no arguments all run. The files the briefs name to read or edit (src/greet.js, test/greet.test.js, docs/index.md, .github/workflows/pages.yml) are all tracked.

Check 2 in the verifier brief breaks the criterion. `git show <base>:bin/greet.js` keeps a literal `<base>` placeholder. In a shell that `<` is read as input redirection from a file named `base`, so the command fails exactly as written. The brief also gives `git worktree add` with no path or commit. Git rejects that and prints a usage error. Both are in backticks as commands to run, and neither has arguments that fit the program.
